name: HyperV
shortdesc: Resource agent for Hyper-V virtual machines
longdesc:
This resource agent manages a Hyper-V virtual machine. On start it
waits for a live migration to complete or imports the VM from its
configuration files on the shared SMB storage if no migration
occurred. On stop it suspends the VM so it can be resumed or
migrated to another node. It also supports live migration via
migrate_to and tracks which node last ran the VM so that failover
after a node crash can be handled correctly.

parameters.name: name
parameters.longdesc: The name of the Hyper-V virtual machine to manage.

parameters.name: metadata_path
parameters.shortdesc: UNC path to VM configuration SMB share
parameters.longdesc:
The UNC path to the SMB share that contains the VM configuration
files (the "Virtual Machines" subdirectory). The share is typically
served by a windows_share resource agent using the cluster service
IP, e.g. \\10.43.208.123\hyper-v-metadata. A vm-state.json file
tracking the VM GUID and last known node is also stored here.

parameters.name: vhd_path
parameters.shortdesc: Path to VHD/VHDX disk image files
parameters.longdesc:
The path to the directory where the VHD/VHDX disk image files are
stored. This is used as the destination when importing the VM after
a failover.

parameters.name: node
parameters.shortdesc: Target node for live migration (set by DRBD reactor)
parameters.longdesc:
The name of the target node to migrate the VM to when the
migrate_to action is invoked. This parameter is set automatically
by the DRBD reactor promoter plugin and does not need to be
specified by the user.

parameters.name: lost_node
parameters.shortdesc: Lost cluster node name (set by DRBD reactor)
parameters.longdesc:
The name of a cluster node that has been declared lost (e.g. it
crashed or lost network connectivity). This parameter is set
automatically by the DRBD reactor promoter plugin and does not
need to be specified by the user. It allows the agent to mark
that node as unavailable in the VM state cache, enabling faster
failover.
